answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it may vote on jobs or claim rewards. The protocol limits each deposit’s influence, so splitting one stake across a thousand accounts does not create a thousand times the voting power; detected collusion or fraudulent claims can burn the locked funds. This makes a sybil attack costly in capital and exposes that capital to loss, rather than letting a vine of fake accounts grow through a canyon of cheap registrations. A pulse of new identities alone earns no influence.
